column1: # The ambient channels a hermetic `git` must not follow, one per line, as behavioural cases.
# Four TAB-separated fields — the channel's name, how it is injected, the observation it moves, and what an
# isolated command reads. Blank lines and lines opening with `#` are prose.
# **One inventory, consumed by every builder.** `kanhe::hermetic_git` owns the isolation and two `shengmo`
# test targets transcribe it, because `kanhe` depends on `shengmo` and the edge would close a cycle. A matrix
# written out per site is a matrix that diverges per site: the first spelling of these cases covered four
# channels in one file and the same four in the other, and the configuration channels beyond
# `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` were in neither. The cases live here so a channel added here is a case every
# builder starts owing.
# An isolated reading that is empty is spelled `(empty)`: a field left blank ends the line with a tab, which
# this repository's whitespace check refuses — and a sentinel a reader decodes is clearer than a field whose
# absence has to be inferred.
# Injection: `git-dir`, `work-tree`, `index` and `config-file` name a path in the decoy repository the
# runner builds; `literal:<value>` is passed as written; `indexed:<key>=<value>` occupies git's indexed
# configuration channel, which is three variables spelling one channel.
# Observation: `log` reads the subject of HEAD, `status` the worktree against the index, `ls-files` the
# index, and `config-probe-marker` the configuration git resolves.
# Each case carries its own control: the same reading taken by a bare `Command` must differ from the
# isolated one, or the case demonstrates no channel and its assertion would hold for the wrong reason.
# **A case names a channel, not one line of the builder.** Deleting a single guard and watching a case is
# what says which line carries it, and two of the answers were not what the builder's own header claimed.
# Measured, one variable at a time:
#   GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM alone removed        still green   -- NOSYSTEM carries it
#   GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM alone removed      still green   -- SYSTEM carries it
#   both removed                           BITES         -- they are redundant with each other
#   GIT_CONFIG_COUNT alone removed         still green
#   GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 alone removed         BITES         -- occupying index 0 is what closes the channel
# So the indexed channel is closed by taking the KEY, not by pinning the COUNT, which is the opposite of
# what `hermetic`'s header said; and the system file has two guards where one would do. Both are recorded
# rather than tidied: redundancy that has been measured is a different fact from redundancy nobody checked.
GIT_DIR
GIT_WORK_TREE
GIT_INDEX_FILE
GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS
GIT_CONFIG
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL
GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT
